goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

However, the guard condition `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` at line 158 (not shown in diff but referenced) would skip reminders that don't meet these conditions without incrementing retryCount. Since the deletion logic at lines 28-43 only removes reminders with retryCount > 1, reminders that fail this guard will never be deleted and will be reconsidered indefinitely. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P2 advisory][confidence 75] The read-derived write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` loses a failure whenever two cron invocations overlap after reading the same count, so the retry ceiling is not enforced; the strongest counterargument that cron normally runs serially fails because this HTTP endpoint has no single-flight guard and each run performs slow external calls before the write.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition. The code reads `reminder.retryCount` at line 57, then later writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` at lines 184 and 193. If two concurrent requests read the same retryCount value before either writes, one increment will be lost. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition. The deletion logic at line 37 deletes reminders where `retryCount > 1`, so if increments are lost, reminders that should be deleted after 2 failures may persist longer. The endpoint is an HTTP handler with no mutex/locking, and the code performs slow external SMS API calls between read and write, making overlap plausible.
